expectations.text: Report file exists at outputs/report.md and is non-empty.
Zero Critical issues and zero High issues are reported.
expectations.evidence: '### Low (defer)' is the only severity bucket. L1 and L2 are Low. No Critical/High.

expectations.text: The report does not fabricate defects: any issues listed are genuinely present in the diff and at most minor (Low) or framed as suggestions/questions.
expectations.evidence: L1 (tests/test_audit.py:18-20 checks key 'email' only; mutation `who=email` passed) and L2 (description claims 'failure paths covered in tests/test_audit.py' but both tests use valid input) are genuine and Low. 'Not reviewed' names pre-existing main issues (float math in billing.charge, no email normalization in charge/lookup); both are real on main (app/billing.py:19 `int(amount * (1 + TAX_RATE_BP / 10_000))`, support.py:7 passes raw email) and explicitly out of scope, not listed as issues. Line ref 'app/billing.py:18' is off by one (actual line 19).

expectations.text: What-was-done-well (or equivalent praise section) credits at least one concrete choice with a file reference, such as audit entries carrying user_id instead of email per CLAUDE.md.
expectations.evidence: '- [`app/users.py:21`] The entry carries `user_id` only. This follows the rule in `CLAUDE.md` that bans raw emails outside the users table.' Plus 3 more file:line credits.

expectations.text: The report is concise — no walls of padded findings; empty severity buckets are left empty or omitted rather than filled.
expectations.evidence: FAILED. The same missing-timestamp finding appears twice: 'Q1 [`app/audit.py:6`] ... The entry holds no time' and 'S1: Put a timestamp in each audit entry ... Locator: `app/audit.py:6`'. The Gaps bucket holds an item the report itself calls harmless: 'Entries collect across test modules. `TestAudit` clears the list itself, so no test fails today.' Every finding bucket (Issues, Questions, Suggestions, Gaps) is filled, and Not reviewed adds two out-of-scope pre-existing defects.

notes: Assertion 5 is subjective; graded as: fail when the same finding is reported in two buckets or a bucket holds an item the report itself says has no effect. All four reports run 62-98 lines for a 31-line diff, mostly because the skill mandates Verified/Not reviewed sections, so raw length alone was not failed. Assertion 3 says 'genuinely present in the diff', yet the strongest genuine findings (no timestamp despite 'who was created and when', commit message overclaiming 'failure paths covered', key-only no-email test) are gaps in the diff, not lines of it; graded as genuine. Assertion 7 path was substituted with the snapshot prose-lint.py per grader instructions. Eval critique: the 'clean' fixture is not fully clean (missing timestamp vs. stated requirement, overclaimed failure-path tests), so Low/Question findings are correct behavior; the assertions cannot tell a well-calibrated Low from filler. Run-specific: strongest empirical evidence (mutation test proving the weak no-email test, bad-input probe), but the most bucket-filling.
